task:
BarrelList is meant to act like list, but many list operations are missing or wrong. For example, BarrelList([1]) == [1] is False, bl.sort(reverse=True) raises TypeError, and bl.extend(bl) never returns. Make all of the following work.

Every rule must hold for a BarrelList built normally and for one split by hand across small sublists, for example bl = BarrelList(); bl.lists = [[5, 3, 8], [1, 9, 3], [7, 2, 6], [0, 4, 3]]. The lists attribute must stay a list of plain lists. In the examples, ref = [5, 3, 8, 1, 9, 3, 7, 2, 6, 0, 4, 3] and bl holds the same items.

Comparison: ==, !=, <, <=, > and >= must follow list comparison against a list or a BarrelList. bl == ref, bl == BarrelList(ref), bl != BarrelList([1]), bl < [6], bl > [5] and BarrelList([1]) < bl are all true. bl != 3 is true and bl == [] is false.

Concatenation and repetition: bl + [1], [1] + bl, bl + bl, bl * 2 and 2 * bl must return plain lists with the same content as the list operations. type(bl + bl) is list. bl += [10] and bl *= 2 must work in place and leave a BarrelList.

Copying: pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(bl)), copy.copy(bl), copy.deepcopy(bl) and a new bl.copy() method must each return a BarrelList with the same items. A round-tripped list must compare equal to the original, including one with 30,000 items spread over many sublists.

index(item, start=0, stop=None) must take bounds exactly as list.index does, including negative bounds. bl.index(3, 2) == 5, bl.index(3, 6) == 11, bl.index(3, -1) == 11, bl.index(3, 6, 12) == 11 and bl.index(3, -7, -1) == 5. These raise ValueError: bl.index(3, 12), bl.index(3, 6, 11), bl.index(8, 3), bl.index(3, 1, 1).

pop must validate arguments as list.pop does: bl.pop(None), bl.pop(1.0) and bl.pop(0, 1) raise TypeError and leave the items unchanged.

New or fixed methods: remove(item) removes the first match. clear() empties the list, so len(bl) == 0. extend(bl) with itself doubles the items and terminates. sort must take keyword-only key and reverse and give exactly the order list.sort gives, including equal items, for example bl.sort(key=lambda x: -x % 5, reverse=True). big.sort(reverse=True) must work on a list spread over many sublists.

Stepped deletion: del bl[start:stop:step] must leave what del on a list leaves, for any mix of None, negative and out-of-range start and stop, and steps including None, -3, -1, 1, 2 and 3, on empty and non-empty lists. With BarrelList(range(8)): del bl[::2] leaves [1, 3, 5, 7], del bl[::-3] leaves [0, 2, 3, 5, 6], and del bl[-2:2:-1] leaves [0, 1, 2, 7].

Everything else must keep working.
accept: PYTHONPATH=.bench-deps python3 -m pytest -q -o addopts= -p no:cacheprovider tests
